name: Ignition
label: Dischord
lede: Two Faith veterans, a Gray Matter drummer and a bassist who sometimes picked up a sax: Ignition spent three years playing sets that could end in wreckage, and left behind twenty-six songs that fit on one CD.

eras.title: The Faith, rewired
eras.text: By 1986 the first wave of D.C. hardcore had burned out and the next one was feeling its way somewhere more melodic and more exposed. Two veterans of Faith decided to try again, one of them on a new instrument.

years.h: Faith's Alec MacKaye and Chris Bald start Ignition
years.p: [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]] reteams with [[Chris Bald|0838359b-95a7-48e9-a9f6-0e8f40bb34d2]], who swaps bass for guitar. [[Dante Ferrando|98b1e2a2-3868-47f0-b905-35637b5a902f]] of [[Iron Cross|13afe528-54f1-4955-bbec-a4bafb590edb]] and [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]] takes the drums, and Dischord's ex-[[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]] man [[Chris Thomson|e79601f0-2aa6-415c-886e-570aea8acea1]] plays bass, with the odd blast of saxophone.
years.xp:
Both front-line members had history. Alec MacKaye, Ian MacKaye's younger brother, was the kid with the X-marked hands on the cover of the Teen Idles' Minor Disturbance, and had sung in the Untouchables and Faith. Chris Bald had followed most of Faith into [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], which had just come apart.

AllMusic dates the start to summer 1986; Dischord just says 1986.

eras.title: Combustible from the first night
eras.text: Ignition came out of the gate as a live band first. The University of Maryland's D.C. punk archive remembers them for chaotic, earnest, combustible shows, and they put out their own singles before Dischord ever gave them an LP number.

years.h: Ignition's first show, at d.c. space
years.p: Dischord dates Ignition's debut to spring 1987 at d.c. space, the downtown D.C. arts space and club.

Ignition's own IG label puts out Anger Means backed with Proven Hollow, produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and engineered by [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]. Discogs lists it as a joint IG/Dischord release, numbered 26½, on blue and gold vinyl.
years.xp: It was one of two early singles. AllMusic names the pair as Sinker and Anger Means and dates them to early 1988; Discogs lists the Anger Means pressings as 1987.

years.p: A benefit at the Wilson Center for Dischord's State of the Union comp: [[Marginal Man|fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca]], Ignition, Fire Party, and a brand-new trio called Fugazi playing its first show. About 300 people paid $5.

years.h: "So Moved" and "Sinker" live in St. Louis, June 3, 1987
yt: "So Moved" and "Sinker" live in St. Louis, June 3, 1987

eras.title: Twelve songs, then six, then gone
eras.text: Ignition toured hard and, per Dischord, became one of the first Dischord bands to play overseas. The shows stayed unpredictable: Dischord recalls one set that ended almost as soon as it started, after Chris Bald damaged his guitar and amp mid-performance. Two records later, it was over.

years.p: Ignition's debut LP: twelve songs cut at Inner Ear in February and May 1988 with Ian MacKaye producing. Dischord dates it to September 1988. A cassette went out the same year.

years.h: Dischord's State of the Union comp arrives, with Ignition on it
years.p: Two years after the 1987 Wilson Center benefit, Dischord 032 is out. Ignition's contribution is Anger Means, alongside [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]], [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]] and [[Fidelity Jones|c6332c9e-a2e3-4d2d-8ad7-a6b3ee837717]].
Six songs from a May 1989 session at Inner Ear, this time with [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] producing. Dischord calls it Ignition's second full-length.
years.xp: AllMusic has it as an EP that appeared in early 1990 and spelled the end of the group. Dischord dates it to 1989.

years.p: The University of Maryland's D.C. punk archive dates Ignition's breakup to 1989. Three years, two LPs, a handful of singles.

eras.title: Everything on one disc
eras.text: The four scattered into some of the most durable projects in the city, including the Black Cat nightclub. Dischord kept the records alive by folding them all onto a single CD, then remastering it for a new generation.

years.h: Where Chris Thomson and Alec MacKaye went next
years.p: Chris Thomson fronts [[Circus Lupus|01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103]], then forms [[The Monorchid|69dbd702-9073-49dd-b73a-67c33f030a4f]] and [[Skull Kontrol|0e327a14-3b74-4635-a9fa-b9060b3acd13]]. Alec MacKaye sings and plays guitar in [[The Warmers|af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f]] with [[Amy Farina|30d1b9a6-4156-49ec-84ba-65c3f5ebbf69]] through the mid-'90s.

years.h: Ignition drummer Dante Ferrando opens the Black Cat
years.p: Dante Ferrando opens the Black Cat on 14th Street in D.C. Pollstar profiled him still running it more than three decades later.
Every Ignition record, all of them originally vinyl or cassette only, on one 26-track CD. Dischord says it also adds an unreleased cover of the Vibrators' Keep It Clean.
Ignition gets a slot on 20 Years of Dischord, the label's three-disc birthday box.
[[TJ Lipple|ed4cd729-b4d2-4016-a0b6-c362b68d2afb]] remasters Ignition's Complete Services CD and Dischord reissues it in limited quantities.

years.h: Alec MacKaye in Salad Days, and at the Phillips Collection
years.p: Alec MacKaye is interviewed in the D.C. punk documentary Salad Days. His day job, per Wikipedia: chief preparator at the Phillips Collection.

sources.title: Pollstar: Clubland, Dante Ferrando and the Black Cat
